relevance_note: Single case report of an infant with a homozygous SLC2A10 variant: 'identified a homozygous pathogenic variant in the SLC2A10 gene'.
method_note: Hand extraction from the paper text; no tables in the paper. In scope: the proband ('patient'); both parents (tested carriers; labelled 'parent of patient' / 'parent of patient 2' because the testing sentence says only 'Both parents', although 'her mother' appears elsewhere); three cousins with diaphragmatic hernias (group statement, labelled 'cousin of patient' 1-3; the paper does not say which side or whether they share the variant, and says only that 'their cousins were undergoing genetic analysis'); and one previously published newborn from reference (9) described in the Discussion with individual-level features and death. Wahab et al. (32 patients), Fadley et al. (12) and Beyens et al. are group-level only and get no rows. The family history of 'cardiac anomalies characterized by tortuous pulmonary arteries' is not attributed to any person and was not recorded. Parents: the paper says they 'carry the same gene', not explicitly the same variant, so their variant rows have variant_original_string 'not reported' and zygosity not reported; proband inheritance left 'not reported' (both parents carriers, homozygous proband; no enum for biparental). Variant type 'missense' taken from the paper's statement that the variant 'causes substitution of the amino acid serine (Ser) with arginine (Arg)'; the paper does not use the word missense. 'loss-of-function mutation' is an assertion without an assay, so functional evidence is not reported. Normal findings: 'vital signs were within normal limits' recorded as 'abnormal vital signs' excluded (does not exclude systemic hypertension); 'without visible deformity' of the chest recorded as 'chest deformity' excluded (pectus left not reported); 'The hernial orifices were intact' recorded as such and inguinal hernia checklist left not reported; obstruction of the aortic arch, head and neck vessels and pulmonary artery branches excluded, so pulmonary artery stenosis excluded, but stenosis of the aorta or aortic branches left not reported because abdominal vessels were not described for stenosis. Aortic root aneurysm excluded from 'tortuosity of the aorta ... without evidence of aneurysmal dilatation' (whole aorta). Age at onset not stated (3 months is age at referral, recorded as onset of poor oral intake only). Dumping syndrome is stated only in the Abstract; the Case section mentions hypoglycemia and octreotide. No contradictions found.

Subsequent genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of ATS.
